response.sql:
WITH per_currency AS (
  SELECT feecoin,
    AVG(CASE WHEN rebtotal <> 0 THEN rebtotal END) AS avg_rebtotal,
    AVG(CASE WHEN feerate <> 0 AND rebrate <> 0 THEN (rebrate - feerate) / feerate END) AS avg_gap
  FROM fees
  GROUP BY feecoin
),
benchmark AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_rebtotal) AS bench FROM per_currency
),
kept AS (
  SELECT p.avg_rebtotal, p.avg_gap, p.avg_rebtotal - b.bench AS excess
  FROM per_currency p
  CROSS JOIN benchmark b
  WHERE p.avg_rebtotal > b.bench
)
SELECT AVG(avg_rebtotal) AS avg_of_avg_rebtotal,
       AVG(avg_gap) AS avg_of_avg_gap,
       AVG(excess) AS avg_excess_over_benchmark
FROM kept;

assumptions.assumption: The relative gap is computed per record as (rebrate - feerate) / feerate, skipping records where feerate or rebrate is 0 or NULL, and then averaged within each currency group.
Fee records with a NULL feecoin form a single group, which GROUP BY produces naturally.
A currency whose average total rebate is NULL (no non-zero, non-NULL rebtotal) is left out of the benchmark and cannot pass the strictly-greater filter, so it is not kept.
If no currency is kept, the final query still returns one row, with NULL values in all three columns.
